rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4, Tables 3-4 <U+2013> the authors build an IoT-based T-shaped sprinkler irrigation prototype (soil moisture, DHT11, rain, wind, water-level sensors on NodeMCU/Arduino), collect about 3,000 records over several months on ThingSpeak, and train KNN, NB, RF, SVM and LR classifiers on pump on/off decisions (accuracy 98.3-99.8%).
rows.notes: The study contains no result on remote sensing, AI-based pest control, disease detection, weed control, crop health monitoring or AgroBots. Its own evidence is limited to in-situ IoT sensors and ML classification of irrigation pump status for an automated sprinkler irrigation prototype in one field. Mentions of disease prediction and pest management appear only in the literature review (citing other work). The technology (ground-based IoT soil/weather sensors for irrigation scheduling) and the effect (irrigation automation / water saving) differ from the claim's remote-sensing-based pest/disease/weed control, so Q2 is 'no' and the cited study does not support the passage.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is a hardware/software prototype plus ML classification study on irrigation automation; it is unrelated to remote sensing for pest control, and the review's citation of it for that claim appears to be a misattribution.
